text: Three o’clock. Gus, Mabel, and Rollo, who had insisted, crouched behind the crates.
The lantern was turned down to a bead. Nobody breathed loudly. Rollo had brought snacks.
Something rose out of it. A hood. Shoulders. A yellow coat, streaming wet, walking up the shelf as if the sea were a staircase.
Three twelve. Far above, the real lamp went dark.
And down here, the stranger lit the other one.
